tropical_outlook: No tropical threat to Jacksonville, Miami or Tampa for Sept 26-27. As of Sept 22 the NHC's only active Atlantic system is Tropical Storm Fay, weakening (~40 mph) over the open North Atlantic and no threat to land; NHC is also monitoring a weak area several hundred miles SW of the Azores with only gradual development possible, far from the U.S. The 2026 Atlantic season has been extremely quiet (NOAA 75% below-normal outlook; no hurricanes to date). Florida rain risk this weekend is non-tropical: an upper-level low / deep tropical moisture that soaked the peninsula on Sept 19-21 is expected to give way to a cooler, drier pattern behind a cold front for the week of Sept 21, so the Sept 27 games face typical late-September sea-breeze storm chances rather than an organized system.
search_caveat: Web search results only exposed aggregator extended forecasts (world-weather.info, weather25, easeweather, AccuWeather monthly) plus local-media articles whose 'Sunday' likely referred to Sept 20, not Sept 27 (several were dated Sept 19-21 and described the cold front that has since passed). Values below labeled 'forecast' come from 5-6 day-out long-range model output and should be refreshed Fri/Sat. Direct weather-site fetches were blocked.
